description: A constructor call that the source writes has an edge: a member initializer (m(1)), a delegation (Delegating(1)), and the call of a default member initializer (Foo m{5}), which keeps its own line and no caller. A construction that the source does not write has no edge: the default construction of a member that the initializer list does not name (n), and the member constructions of an implicit constructor (imp, nest, local). That gap is known and intended: a derivation by the rules of C++ was measured and dropped. When a later layer fills it, this truth changes.
